messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> Prefix-cache miss-rate alert (us-west-2). 95th latency for text-gen increased, customer-facing errors observed. Paging: @Jamie (oncall).

Jamie (oncall): oncall here, ack. I'm looking at the gateway error spikes now. ETA 5m. Any initial hypothesis?

Mike SRE: seeing 5xx tail latencies at the inference gateway, correlated with a sharp rise in prefix cache misses. Graphs: prefix_cache_miss_rate jumped from ~12% -> ~48% around 2073456650. Customer impact: intermittent timeouts for DocuFlow and a few other mid-market tenants.

Luis (observability): pulling logs and metrics now. PromQL I'm using: `sum(rate(prefix_cache_misses[1m])) / sum(rate(prefix_cache_lookups[1m]))` and `sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m]))`. Early outputs: misses 0.47, evictions spiked to 820/s at peak.

Angela (prod-eng): we rolled the hashed-prefix change in us-west-2 at 2073456571 (canary -> full) — could be related. That change altered key normalization for some tenant prefixes.

Tal (infra): also seeing a Redis replica failover around 2073456620 for cache-shard-3. Failover logs show a ~30s window where writes queued. Could cause TTL/consistency gaps.

Mike SRE: building a quick timeline here (rough):
- 2073456571: hashed-prefix rollout completed (canary -> global)
- 2073456620: cache-shard-3 Redis replica failover event
- 2073456650: prefix_cache_miss_rate spike begins
- 2073456705: gateway 95th latency crosses SLA threshold -> pager
- 2073456730: initial autoscale + rewarm attempts kicked off
- 2073456800: manual routing change to fallback model for critical customers

Jamie (oncall): that timeline + change windows makes me suspect a coordination issue: prefix key normalization change + a transient failover could cause many cache keys to be treated as new (cache misses) and trigger eviction pressure. Hypothesis A: hashed-prefix rollout changed lookup key shape, causing near-zero KV reuse for older cached keys while eviction storm reduced capacity.

Angela (prod-eng): Agree. Another angle: the invalidation job that runs post-rollout had a bug where it issued wide-prefix invalidations without token-bucket rate limiting — if that ran while failover happened, it could amplify misses. Checking job logs now.

Luis (observability): pulled logs from the invalidation job: snippet: 
```
2026-11-06T12:50:20Z job-worker-12 INFO invalidating prefix=docuflow:,pattern=full,issued=120000
2026-11-06T12:50:21Z job-worker-12 WARN redis timeout on shard-3, retrying
2026-11-06T12:50:22Z job-worker-12 INFO invalidation-batch-complete duration=1.1s
```
Looks like it attempted broad invalidation with large batch sizes exactly around failover.

Mike SRE: sharing a live log tail from gateway showing cache misses per request: 
```
[2073456651] req_id=abc123 prefix=docuflow:user:miss cache_lookup=0 backend_fetch=1 latency_ms=1120
[2073456651] req_id=abc124 prefix=docuflow:widget:miss cache_lookup=0 backend_fetch=1 latency_ms=980
[2073456652] req_id=abc125 prefix=docuflow:user:miss cache_lookup=0 backend_fetch=1 latency_ms=1500
```

Jamie (oncall): Mitigation options considered:
- Temp route critical customers to fallback model pool (done at 2073456800) -> reduced error rate for DocuFlow by ~60%
- Pause invalidation job (requested) -> pending ops approval
- Run targeted warmup for high-volume prefixes (backfill) -> scheduling now
- Increase cache TTL or temp enlarge capacity -> infra action item

Tal (infra): spun up an extra Redis replica for shard-3 and increased maxmemory for the cluster to reduce immediate evictions. Also applied a temporary rate-limit on invalidation job via feature flag.

ops-shiftbot: ACTION: invalidation_job.pause flagged=true by Tal at 2073456785 :gear:

Angela (prod-eng): starting targeted warmup for DocuFlow prefixes. Command: 
```
python tools/warm_cache.py --prefix docuflow: --concurrency 50 --max-keys 100000
```
Warmup started 2073456792.

Mike SRE: collecting sample of keys and running reuse check: `redis-cli -c -h shard-3 --scan --pattern "docuflow:*" | wc -l` -> found ~120k keys but with new hashed keys mostly empty TTL or missing values -> supports normalization mismatch.

Luis (observability): plotting hit-rate timeline and attaching quick numbers: pre-rollout (1h window) avg hit-rate=0.88, post-rollout spike window hit-rate=0.52, worst 0.34 at peak.

Jamie (oncall): summary so far for incident channel:
- Customer impact: intermittent timeouts for ~4 high-volume tenants (DocuFlow highest), user-facing errors and higher latencies.
- Root hypothesis: combination of hashed-prefix key shape change + invalidation job running during Redis failover -> mass cache misses + eviction storm -> increased backend load and 5xx/timeouts.
- Immediate mitigations: fallback routing for critical tenants (done), invalidate_job paused (done), targeted warmup started (in progress), extra Redis capacity (done).

Angela (prod-eng): moving to handoff. I will own follow-up on key normalization rollout and fix the invalidation job batching. ETA for fix and re-rollback plan: 6 hours.

Jamie (oncall): handing over to Angela at 2073456845, I need rest-of-shift log collection. I'll update runbook with what we observed.

Mike SRE: I'll own the warmup script monitoring and verify hit-rate returns to baseline. Will post back metrics every 10m.

Luis (observability): capture for RCA: full metric dump + grafana panels saved -> link: https://grafana.internal/shot/abcd1234 (internal).

Tal (infra): follow-ups: add safety checks to invalidation job (rate limit + shard-healthy-check), add automated rollback for prefix-normalization change if hit-rate drop >20% in 10m post-rollout.

Jamie (oncall): adding checklist items here so RCA thread has owners:
- Angela: fix invalidation-job batching + rollout rollback plan (owner)
- Mike: warmup monitoring + verification (owner)
- Tal: infra safeties and add rollback automation (owner)
- Luis: compile timeline + metric attachments for postmortem (owner)

Angela (prod-eng): quick note on customer comms: recommend status update to affected customers indicating degraded performance and that we've implemented mitigations; follow-up with root cause and timeline after RCA.

ops-shiftbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, severity downgraded to P2 at 2073456858.

Jamie (oncall): good work team. Leaving thread in Angela's hands for RCA write-up. If anyone finds contrary evidence to the hypothesis, ping me. :white_check_mark:
